740	def _metric_precision(metric_selector: str) -> int:
741	    # Higher = more specific: exact name > glob pattern > bare "*".
742	    if "*" not in metric_selector:
743	        return 2
744	    if metric_selector == "*":
745	        return 0
746	    return 1
747	
748	
749	def _metric_matches(metric_selector: str, name: str) -> bool:
750	    if "*" not in metric_selector:
751	        return metric_selector == name
752	    pattern = "^" + "".join(".*" if ch == "*" else re.escape(ch) for ch in metric_selector) + "$"
753	    return re.match(pattern, name) is not None

756	def _validate_suppression_rule(raw: Any, seen_rule_ids: set) -> dict:
757	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
758	        raise ValueError("invalid suppression rule")
759	    rule_id = raw.get("rule_id")
760	    if not (isinstance(rule_id, str) and rule_id != ""):
761	        raise ValueError("invalid rule_id")
762	    if rule_id in seen_rule_ids:
763	        raise ValueError("duplicate rule_id")
764	    selector = _validate_selector(raw.get("selector"))
765	    min_severity = raw.get("min_severity")
766	    if min_severity not in SEVERITY_ORDER:
767	        raise ValueError("invalid severity")
768	    duration = raw.get("suppression_ms")
769	    if not (_is_int(duration) and duration >= 0):
770	        raise ValueError("invalid suppression_ms")
771	    seen_rule_ids.add(rule_id)
772	    return {
773	        "rule_id": rule_id,
774	        "selector": selector,
775	        "min_severity": min_severity,
776	        "suppression_ms": duration,
777	    }

780	def _select_rule(alert: dict, rules: list) -> dict | None:
781	    """Pick the best rule matching an alert.
782	
783	    Priority: more matched label conditions, then more specific metric selector,
784	    then the lexicographically smallest rule_id.
785	    """
786	    best = None
787	    best_key = None
788	    for rule in rules:
789	        selector = rule["selector"]
790	        if not _metric_matches(selector["metric"], alert["name"]):
791	            continue
792	        label_matchers = selector["labels"]
793	        alert_labels = alert["labels"]
794	        if any(alert_labels.get(key) != value for key, value in label_matchers.items()):
795	            continue
796	        if SEVERITY_ORDER[alert["severity"]] < SEVERITY_ORDER[rule["min_severity"]]:
797	            continue
798	        rank_key = (len(label_matchers), _metric_precision(selector["metric"]))
799	        if best is None or rank_key > best_key or (rank_key == best_key and rule["rule_id"] < best["rule_id"]):
800	            best = rule
801	            best_key = rank_key
802	    return best

805	class ExplanationRegistry:
806	    """Stores suppression explanation records across processed batches."""
807	
808	    def __init__(self) -> None:
809	        self._records: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
810	
811	    def add_all(self, records: list) -> None:
812	        for record in records:
813	            identity = (
814	                record["suppressed_fingerprint"],
815	                record["suppressor_fingerprint"],
816	                record["rule_id"],
817	                record["started_at"],
818	                record["expires_at"],
819	            )
820	            self._records[identity] = dict(record)
821	
822	    def query(
823	        self,
824	        fingerprint: str | None = None,
825	        rule_id: str | None = None,
826	        now_ms: Any = None,
827	    ) -> list:
828	        if now_ms is None:
829	            current_ms = time.time() * 1000.0
830	        else:
831	            if not (_is_number(now_ms) and math.isfinite(now_ms) and now_ms >= 0):
832	                raise ValueError("invalid now_ms")
833	            current_ms = now_ms
834	
835	        result = []
836	        for record in self._records.values():
837	            if fingerprint is not None and record["suppressed_fingerprint"] != fingerprint:
838	                continue
839	            if rule_id is not None and record["rule_id"] != rule_id:
840	                continue
841	            view = dict(record)
842	            # End time is reported only once known; it is never guessed up front.
843	            if current_ms >= record["expires_at"]:
844	                view["ended_at"] = record["expires_at"]
845	            result.append(view)
846	        result.sort(
847	            key=lambda r: (
848	                r["started_at"],
849	                r["rule_id"],
850	                r["suppressed_fingerprint"],
851	                r["suppressor_fingerprint"],
852	            )
853	        )
854	        return result
855	
856	    def clear(self) -> None:
857	        self._records.clear()
858

872	    include ended_at. An unknown fingerprint or rule_id yields an empty list.

883	def _rule_suppressions(alerts: list, rules: list) -> tuple[list, list, dict]:
884	    """Pure rule-based adjudication.
885	
886	    Returns ``(labels_keys, fingerprints, suppression_by_index)`` where the
887	    mapping is ``alert index -> (started_at, suppressor_index, rule)``. Has no
888	    side effects, so audit callers can run it without touching an
889	    ``ExplanationRegistry``.
890	    """
891	    labels_keys = [_canonical_labels(alert["labels"]) for alert in alerts]
892	    fingerprints = [
893	        alert_fingerprint(alert["name"], alert["labels"], alert["timestamp_ms"])
894	        for alert in alerts
895	    ]
896	
897	    # Chronological adjudication per metric (name + full label set), mirroring
898	    # the baseline ordering (timestamp_ms, then alert_id). Each chain holds the
899	    # previously valid (active) alerts that can still act as suppressors.
900	    order = sorted(
901	        range(len(alerts)),
902	        key=lambda i: (alerts[i]["timestamp_ms"], alerts[i]["alert_id"]),
903	    )
904	    chains: dict = {}
905	    suppression_by_index: dict = {}
906	
907	    for index in order:
908	        alert = alerts[index]
909	        timestamp_ms = alert["timestamp_ms"]
910	        severity = SEVERITY_ORDER[alert["severity"]]
911	        rule = _select_rule(alert, rules)
912	        suppressor = None
913	        if rule is not None:
914	            duration = rule["suppression_ms"]
915	            chain = chains.get((alert["name"], labels_keys[index]), ())
916	            for anchor_ts, anchor_alert_id, anchor_severity, anchor_index in reversed(chain):
917	                if anchor_ts > timestamp_ms or (
918	                    anchor_ts == timestamp_ms and anchor_alert_id >= alert["alert_id"]
919	                ):
920	                    continue
921	                if timestamp_ms - anchor_ts > duration:
922	                    break  # every remaining anchor is even older
923	                if timestamp_ms == anchor_ts and severity > anchor_severity:
924	                    # Same-fingerprint duplicates keep the existing adjudication
925	                    # semantics: a higher severity breaks through at a tie.
926	                    break
927	                suppressor = (anchor_ts, anchor_index, rule)
928	                break
929	
930	        if suppressor is None:
931	            chains.setdefault((alert["name"], labels_keys[index]), []).append(
932	                (timestamp_ms, alert["alert_id"], severity, index)
933	            )
934	        else:
935	            suppression_by_index[index] = suppressor
936	
937	    return labels_keys, fingerprints, suppression_by_index
938

940	def _process_with_explanations(
941	    alerts: list,
942	    series: list,
943	    rules: list,
944	    registry: ExplanationRegistry,
945	) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
946	    _labels_keys, fingerprints, suppression_by_index = _rule_suppressions(alerts, rules)
947	
948	    output_alerts = []
949	    explanations = []
950	    suppressed_alert_ids: list = []
951	    rule_hit_by_index: dict = {}
952	
953	    # Output keeps the original alert fields and input order.
954	    for index, alert in enumerate(alerts):
955	        output_alert = {field: alert[field] for field in _ALERT_FIELDS}
956	        output_alert["fingerprint"] = fingerprints[index]
957	        suppression = suppression_by_index.get(index)
958	        if suppression is None:
959	            output_alert["status"] = "active"
960	        else:
961	            started_at, suppressor_index, rule = suppression
962	            output_alert["status"] = "suppressed"
963	            suppressed_alert_ids.append(alert["alert_id"])
964	            rule_hit_by_index[index] = rule["rule_id"]
965	            explanations.append(
966	                {
967	                    "suppressed_fingerprint": fingerprints[index],
968	                    "suppressor_fingerprint": fingerprints[suppressor_index],
969	                    "rule_id": rule["rule_id"],
970	                    "started_at": started_at,
971	                    "expires_at": started_at + rule["suppression_ms"],
972	                }
973	            )
974	        output_alerts.append(output_alert)
975	
976	    # Commit explanations only after the whole batch has been produced.
977	    registry.add_all(explanations)
978	
979	    result = {
980	        "series": series,
981	        "alerts": output_alerts,
982	        "suppressed_alert_ids": suppressed_alert_ids,
983	        "explanations": explanations,
984	    }
985	    return result, rule_hit_by_index

1061	def _validate_window_rule(raw: Any, seen_rule_ids: set) -> dict:
1062	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
1063	        raise RuleConfigurationError("invalid window suppression rule")
1064	    rule_id = raw.get("rule_id")
1065	    if not (isinstance(rule_id, str) and rule_id != ""):
1066	        raise RuleConfigurationError("invalid rule_id")
1067	    if rule_id in seen_rule_ids:
1068	        raise RuleConfigurationError("duplicate rule_id")
1069	    source = raw.get("source")
1070	    if not (isinstance(source, str) and source != ""):
1071	        raise RuleConfigurationError("invalid source")
1072	    metric = raw.get("metric")
1073	    if not (isinstance(metric, str) and metric != ""):
1074	        raise RuleConfigurationError("invalid metric")
1075	    labels = raw.get("labels", {})
1076	    if labels is None:
1077	        labels = {}
1078	    if not isinstance(labels, dict):
1079	        raise RuleConfigurationError("invalid labels")
1080	    for key, value in labels.items():
1081	        if not (isinstance(key, str) and key != "" and isinstance(value, str)):
1082	            raise RuleConfigurationError("invalid labels")
1083	    pending_ms = raw.get("pending_ms")
1084	    if not (_is_int(pending_ms) and pending_ms >= 0):
1085	        raise RuleConfigurationError("invalid pending_ms")
1086	    suppression_ms = raw.get("suppression_ms")
1087	    if not (_is_int(suppression_ms) and suppression_ms >= 0):

1135	class WindowSuppressionEngine:
1136	    """Event-time state machine for time-window suppression rules.
1137	
1138	    One episode is tracked per ``(rule_id, source, canonical labels)``; label
1139	    combinations never influence each other. Matching events accumulate over
1140	    ``pending_ms`` before the episode turns ``suppressed``; the suppression
1141	    window never extends on repeated matches. Once ``suppression_ms`` has
1142	    elapsed the episode is in recovery observation: a match restarts the
1143	    observation (the recorded suppression end stays untouched), and only a
1144	    full quiet ``recovery_ms`` returns the combination to ``missed``.
1145	    """
1146	
1147	    def __init__(self, rules: list | None = None) -> None:
1148	        self._rules: list = []
1149	        self._states: dict = {}
1150	        self._last_event_time = None
1151	        if rules is not None:
1152	            self.set_rules(rules)
1153	
1154	    @property
1155	    def rules(self) -> list:
1156	        return [dict(rule, labels=dict(rule["labels"])) for rule in self._rules]
1157	
1158	    def set_rules(self, rules: list | None) -> None:
1159	        """Replace the rule set; takes effect for the next incoming event.
1160	
1161	        Already recorded episodes are kept untouched: changed durations never
1162	        retroactively alter recorded hits, and states of removed rules stay
1163	        queryable by rule_id — removal only stops future matching.
1164	        """
1165	        validated = _validate_window_rules(rules)
1166	        self._rules = validated
1167	
1168	    def reset(self) -> None:
1169	        """Drop all recorded episodes; the configured rules are kept."""
1170	        self._states = {}
1171	        self._last_event_time = None
1172	
1173	    # -- event intake ---------------------------------------------------------
1174	
1175	    def record_event(self, event: dict) -> None:
1176	        """Feed one observation (metric sample or alert) into the engine."""
1177	        if not isinstance(event, dict) or event.get("timestamp_ms") is None:
1178	            raise RuleConfigurationError("missing event timestamp")
1179	        timestamp_ms = event["timestamp_ms"]
1180	        if not _valid_timestamp(timestamp_ms):
1181	            raise EventTimestampError("unsortable event timestamp")
1182	        if self._last_event_time is None or timestamp_ms > self._last_event_time:
1183	            self._last_event_time = timestamp_ms
1184	        source = event.get("source")
1185	        name = event.get("name")
1186	        labels = event.get("labels")
1187	        if not (
1188	            isinstance(source, str)
1189	            and source != ""
1190	            and isinstance(name, str)
1191	            and isinstance(labels, dict)
1192	        ):
1193	            return
1194	        labels_key = _canonical_labels(labels)
1195	        for rule in self._matching_rules(source, name, labels):
1196	            key = (rule["rule_id"], source, labels_key)
1197	            state = self._states.get(key)
1198	            if state is None:
1199	                state = _WindowComboState(labels)
1200	                self._states[key] = state
1201	            self._advance(state, timestamp_ms, rule)
1202	
1203	    def _matching_rules(self, source: str, name: str, labels: dict):
1204	        for rule in self._rules:
1205	            if rule["source"] != source:
1206	                continue
1207	            if not _metric_matches(rule["metric"], name):
1208	                continue
1209	            if any(labels.get(key) != value for key, value in rule["labels"].items()):
1210	                continue
1211	            yield rule
1212	
1213	    def _advance(self, state: _WindowComboState, timestamp_ms: Any, rule: dict) -> None:
1214	        if state.suppression_end is not None:
1215	            if timestamp_ms <= state.suppression_end:
1216	                # Inside the suppression window: repeated matches never
1217	                # extend it.
1218	                return
1219	            if timestamp_ms <= state.recovery_deadline:
1220	                # A match during recovery restarts the observation; the
1221	                # recorded suppression end stays unchanged.
1222	                state.recovery_deadline = timestamp_ms + rule["recovery_ms"]
1223	                return
1224	            # Recovery completed quietly: the episode is over and this event
1225	            # starts a fresh observation run.
1226	            state.suppression_start = None
1227	            state.suppression_end = None
1228	            state.recovery_deadline = None
1229	            state.run_start = None
1230	        if state.run_start is None:
1231	            state.run_start = timestamp_ms
1232	            state.active_start = timestamp_ms
1233	        if timestamp_ms - state.run_start >= rule["pending_ms"]:
1234	            state.suppression_start = timestamp_ms
1235	            state.suppression_end = timestamp_ms + rule["suppression_ms"]
1236	            state.recovery_deadline = state.suppression_end + rule["recovery_ms"]
1237	
1238	    # -- suppression decisions --------------------------------------------------
1239	
1240	    def _suppressing_windows(
1241	        self, source: str, name: str, labels: dict, timestamp_ms: Any
1242	    ) -> list:
1243	        """Matching rule episodes actively suppressing an alert at ``timestamp_ms``.
1244	
1245	        Returns ``(rule_id, suppression_end)`` pairs (in rule iteration order)
1246	        for every matching rule whose episode covers the timestamp. The
1247	        aggregate boolean follows the pair with the earliest end; audit
1248	        callers keep every pair so each hitting rule_id can be listed.
1249	        """
1250	        if not (
1251	            isinstance(source, str)
1252	            and isinstance(name, str)
1253	            and isinstance(labels, dict)
1254	            and _valid_timestamp(timestamp_ms)
1255	        ):
1256	            return []
1257	        labels_key = _canonical_labels(labels)
1258	        windows = []
1259	        for rule in self._matching_rules(source, name, labels):
1260	            state = self._states.get((rule["rule_id"], source, labels_key))
1261	            if state is None or state.suppression_end is None:
1262	                continue
1263	            if not (state.suppression_start <= timestamp_ms <= state.recovery_deadline):
1264	                continue
1265	            windows.append((rule["rule_id"], state.suppression_end))
1266	        return windows
1267	
1268	    def is_suppressed(self, source: str, name: str, labels: dict, timestamp_ms: Any) -> bool:
1269	        """Whether an alert emitted at ``timestamp_ms`` is suppressed.
1270	
1271	        When several rules hit the same event, the aggregate follows the
1272	        suppression window with the earliest end.
1273	        """
1274	        windows = self._suppressing_windows(source, name, labels, timestamp_ms)
1275	        if not windows:
1276	            return False
1277	        earliest_end = min(end for _rule_id, end in windows)
1278	        return timestamp_ms <= earliest_end
1279	
1280	    def suppressing_rules(self, source: str, name: str, labels: dict, timestamp_ms: Any) -> list:
1281	        """rule_ids of window rules actively suppressing an alert (sorted).
1282	
1283	        Mirrors ``is_suppressed`` exactly — ``bool(result)`` equals the
1284	        aggregate verdict: once the earliest-ending covering window has
1285	        expired the alert breaks through, so even another still-open window
1286	        is not reported as a cause.
1287	        """
1288	        windows = self._suppressing_windows(source, name, labels, timestamp_ms)
1289	        if not windows:
1290	            return []
1291	        earliest_end = min(end for _rule_id, end in windows)
1292	        if timestamp_ms > earliest_end:
1293	            return []
1294	        return sorted(rule_id for rule_id, _end in windows)
1295	
1296	    # -- queries ----------------------------------------------------------------
1297	
1298	    def query(
1299	        self,
1300	        rule_id: str | None = None,
1301	        source: str | None = None,
1302	        labels: dict | None = None,
1303	        now_ms: Any = None,
1304	    ) -> list:
1305	        """Return recorded suppression states, sorted by rule_id/source/labels.
1306	
1307	        ``now_ms`` defaults to the latest event time seen by the engine, so
1308	        adjudication stays on the event-time axis.
1309	        """
1310	        if now_ms is None:
1311	            now = self._last_event_time if self._last_event_time is not None else 0
1312	        elif _valid_timestamp(now_ms):
1313	            now = now_ms
1314	        else:
1315	            raise EventTimestampError("unsortable event timestamp")
1316	        records = []
1317	        for (state_rule_id, state_source, _labels_key), state in self._states.items():
1318	            if rule_id is not None and state_rule_id != rule_id:
1319	                continue
1320	            if source is not None and state_source != source:
1321	                continue
1322	            if labels is not None and any(
1323	                state.labels.get(key) != value for key, value in labels.items()
1324	            ):
1325	                continue
1326	            records.append(
1327	                {
1328	                    "rule_id": state_rule_id,
1329	                    "source": state_source,
1330	                    "labels": dict(state.labels),
1331	                    "active_start_ms": state.active_start,
1332	                    "suppression_end_ms": state.suppression_end,
1333	                    "status": self._status_of(state, now),
1334	                }
1335	            )
1336	        records.sort(
1337	            key=lambda record: (
1338	                record["rule_id"],
1339	                record["source"],
1340	                _canonical_labels(record["labels"]),
1341	            )
1342	        )
1343	        return records
1344	
1345	    @staticmethod
1346	    def _status_of(state: _WindowComboState, now: Any) -> str:
1347	        if state.suppression_end is not None:
1348	            if now <= state.suppression_end:
1349	                return WINDOW_STATUS_SUPPRESSED
1350	            if now <= state.recovery_deadline:
1351	                return WINDOW_STATUS_RECOVERED
1352	            return WINDOW_STATUS_MISSED
1353	        if state.run_start is not None:
1354	            return WINDOW_STATUS_PENDING
1355	        return WINDOW_STATUS_MISSED

1378	def _feed_window_events(engine: WindowSuppressionEngine, metrics: list, alerts: list) -> tuple[set, dict]:
1379	    """Drive the engine with one batch of events in event-time order.
1380	
1381	    Returns ``(suppressed_ids, rule_hits_by_alert)``: the ids of alerts
1382	    suppressed by a window rule, together with the sorted rule_ids that hit
1383	    each suppressed alert. An alert is evaluated against the state right
1384	    before its own event is recorded, so the observation that triggers a
1385	    suppression is still emitted and only later observations are suppressed.
1386	    """
1387	    events = [(metric["timestamp_ms"], index, metric, None) for index, metric in enumerate(metrics)]
1388	    events += [
1389	        (alert["timestamp_ms"], len(metrics) + index, alert, alert["alert_id"])
1390	        for index, alert in enumerate(alerts)
1391	    ]
1392	    events.sort(key=lambda event: (event[0], event[1]))
1393	    suppressed_ids: set = set()
1394	    rule_hits_by_alert: dict = {}
1395	    for timestamp_ms, _index, event, alert_id in events:
1396	        if alert_id is not None:
1397	            hit_rules = engine.suppressing_rules(
1398	                event["source"], event["name"], event["labels"], timestamp_ms
1399	            )
1400	            if hit_rules:
1401	                suppressed_ids.add(alert_id)
1402	                rule_hits_by_alert[alert_id] = hit_rules
1403	        engine.record_event(event)
1404	    return suppressed_ids, rule_hits_by_alert

1428	        raise MaintenanceWindowError("invalid maintenance_window")

1441	                raise MaintenanceWindowError("invalid maintenance_window")

1444	        raise MaintenanceWindowError("invalid maintenance_window")

1508	def process(
1509	    request: dict,
1510	    *,
1511	    registry: ExplanationRegistry | None = None,
1512	    window_engine: WindowSuppressionEngine | None = None,
1513	) -> dict:
1514	    """Fuse metrics and alerts from a request mapping into a response mapping."""
1515	    if not isinstance(request, dict):
1516	        raise ValueError("invalid request")
1517	
1518	    downsample_ms = request.get("downsample_ms")
1519	    if not _is_int(downsample_ms) or downsample_ms <= 0:
1520	        raise ValueError("invalid downsample_ms")
1521	    suppression_ms = request.get("suppression_ms")
1522	    if not _is_int(suppression_ms) or suppression_ms < 0:
1523	        raise ValueError("invalid suppression_ms")
1524	
1525	    # Per-metric aggregation selection; validated before any state is touched
1526	    # so a failure leaves nothing partially applied.
1527	    aggregations = _validate_aggregations(request.get("aggregations"))
1528	
1529	    # Optional per-metric source coverage thresholds; validated up front for
1530	    # the same all-or-nothing reason as aggregations.
1531	    source_quorum = _validate_source_quorum(request.get("source_quorum"))
1532	
1533	    # Optional per-target source weights; validated up front (all or nothing)
1534	    # so a rejected configuration leaves nothing partially applied. Targets
1535	    # absent from the mapping keep the default equal-weight merge.
1536	    source_weights = _validate_source_weights(request.get("source_weights"))
1537	
1538	    # Optional per-target ordered source failover; validated up front like the
1539	    # other per-metric query options. The same metric target cannot be tuned by
1540	    # both weights and priority.
1541	    source_priority = _validate_source_priority(request.get("source_priority"))
1542	    if source_priority.keys() & source_weights.keys():
1543	        raise ValueError("invalid source_priority")
1544	
1545	    # Optional per-metric gap filling of the series output; validated up front
1546	    # (all or nothing) like every other optional query configuration.
1547	    gap_fill = _validate_gap_fill(request.get("gap_fill"))
1548	
1549	    # Optional per-metric downsample periods overriding downsample_ms for
1550	    # series windowing only; validated up front (all or nothing) so a rejected
1551	    # configuration leaves nothing partially applied.
1552	    downsample_overrides = _validate_downsample_overrides(request.get("downsample_overrides"))
1553	
1554	    # Optional per-metric source-outlier filtering of series windows;
1555	    # validated up front (all or nothing) like every other optional query
1556	    # configuration. Metrics absent from the mapping are unaffected.
1557	    source_outliers = _validate_source_outliers(request.get("source_outliers"))
1558	
1559	    # The explanation subsystem is fully dormant unless explicitly enabled,
1560	    # so legacy inputs, outputs and error behavior stay untouched.
1561	    enabled_raw = request.get("enable_explanations", False)
1562	    if not isinstance(enabled_raw, bool):
1563	        raise ValueError("invalid enable_explanations")
1564	    enabled = enabled_raw
1565	
1566	    # The suppression audit is opt-in and strictly boolean; any other value
1567	    # type (including strings and 1/0) is rejected up front so a failure never
1568	    # leaves partially applied state.
1569	    include_audit_raw = request.get("include_suppression_audit", False)
1570	    if not isinstance(include_audit_raw, bool):
1571	        raise ValueError("invalid suppression audit")
1572	    include_audit = include_audit_raw
1573	    rules: list = []
1574	    if enabled:
1575	        raw_rules = request.get("suppression_rules", [])
1576	        if raw_rules is None:
1577	            raw_rules = []
1578	        if not isinstance(raw_rules, list):
1579	            raise ValueError("invalid suppression rules")
1580	        seen_rule_ids: set = set()
1581	        rules = [_validate_suppression_rule(raw, seen_rule_ids) for raw in raw_rules]
1582	
1583	    # Time-window suppression rules stay dormant unless the request carries
1584	    # them; they are validated (all or nothing) up front and only become
1585	    # effective once the whole request has passed validation.
1586	    raw_window_rules = request.get("window_suppression_rules")
1587	    validated_window_rules: list | None = None
1588	    if raw_window_rules is not None:
1589	        validated_window_rules = _validate_window_rules(raw_window_rules)
1590	
1591	    # Maintenance windows stay dormant unless the request carries them; they
1592	    # are validated (all or nothing) up front like every other optional config.
1593	    maintenance_windows = _validate_maintenance_windows(request.get("maintenance_windows"))
1594	
1595	    raw_metrics = request.get("metrics")
1596	    raw_alerts = request.get("alerts")
1597	    if not isinstance(raw_metrics, list) or not isinstance(raw_alerts, list):
1598	        raise ValueError("invalid request")
1599	
1600	    metrics = [_validate_metric(metric) for metric in raw_metrics]
1601	    seen_ids: set = set()
1602	    alerts = [_validate_alert(alert, seen_ids) for alert in raw_alerts]
1603	
1604	    series = _downsample(
1605	        metrics,
1606	        downsample_ms,
1607	        aggregations,
1608	        source_quorum,
1609	        source_weights,
1610	        source_priority,
1611	        gap_fill,
1612	        downsample_overrides,
1613	        source_outliers,
1614	    )
1615	
1616	    window_suppressed_ids: set = set()
1617	    window_rule_hits: dict = {}
1618	    engine: WindowSuppressionEngine | None = None
1619	    if validated_window_rules is not None:
1620	        engine = _default_window_engine if window_engine is None else window_engine
1621	        engine.set_rules(validated_window_rules)
1622	        window_suppressed_ids, window_rule_hits = _feed_window_events(engine, metrics, alerts)
1623	
1624	    maintenance_suppressed_ids = _maintenance_suppressed_ids(alerts, maintenance_windows)
1625	    extra_suppressed_ids = window_suppressed_ids | maintenance_suppressed_ids
1626	
1627	    result_alerts, _suppressed_alert_ids, time_suppressed_ids = _suppress_alerts(
1628	        alerts, suppression_ms
1629	    )
1630	    final_suppressed_ids = set(time_suppressed_ids)
1631	    if extra_suppressed_ids:
1632	        for entry in result_alerts:
1633	            if entry["alert_id"] in extra_suppressed_ids:
1634	                entry["suppressed"] = True
1635	        final_suppressed_ids |= extra_suppressed_ids
1636	    suppressed_alert_ids = [

# covers the point.
_LATE_RANK = (0, "")


class BatchError(ValueError):
    """Structured batch-API failure carrying an HTTP status and a stable code."""

    def __init__(self, status: int, code: str, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.code = code


def _canonical_sample(metric: dict) -> str:
    return json.dumps(
        {
            "source": metric["source"],
            "name": metric["name"],
            "labels": metric["labels"],
            "timestamp_ms": metric["timestamp_ms"],
            "value": metric["value"],
        },
        sort_keys=True,
        ensure_ascii=False,
        separators=(",", ":"),
    )


def _canonical_alert(alert: dict) -> str:
    return json.dumps(
        {field: alert[field] for field in _ALERT_FIELDS},
        sort_keys=True,
        ensure_ascii=False,
        separators=(",", ":"),
    )


def _batch_fingerprint(max_event_time_ms: Any, metrics: list, alerts: list) -> str:
    """Content fingerprint of a batch, independent of sample ordering."""
    payload = "\n".join(
        ["v1", repr(max_event_time_ms)]
        + sorted(_canonical_sample(metric) for metric in metrics)
        + ["--"]
        + sorted(_canonical_alert(alert) for alert in alerts)
    )
    return hashlib.sha256(payload.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


class MetricBatchService:
    """Stateful metric-stream store accepting idempotent, order-independent batches.

    Samples are kept per stream so that late batches recompute exactly the
    downsample windows they touch; queries always reflect the current state.
    Point conflicts across batches resolve deterministically by batch rank
    ``(max_event_time_ms, batch_id)`` — the higher rank wins — so the final
    aggregates do not depend on batch arrival order. Individual late samples
    (``submit_late_metrics``) recompute only the windows they touch and reject
    identity conflicts instead of ranking them.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        downsample_ms: int | None = None,
        suppression_ms: int = 0,
        suppression_rules: list | None = None,
        enable_explanations: bool = False,
        registry: ExplanationRegistry | None = None,
        window_suppression_rules: list | None = None,
        maintenance_windows: list | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if downsample_ms is not None and (not _is_int(downsample_ms) or downsample_ms <= 0):
            raise ValueError("invalid downsample_ms")
        if not _is_int(suppression_ms) or suppression_ms < 0:
            raise ValueError("invalid suppression_ms")
        if not isinstance(enable_explanations, bool):
            raise ValueError("invalid enable_explanations")
        rules: list = []
        if enable_explanations:
            raw_rules = [] if suppression_rules is None else suppression_rules
            if not isinstance(raw_rules, list):
                raise ValueError("invalid suppression rules")
            seen_rule_ids: set = set()
            rules = [_validate_suppression_rule(raw, seen_rule_ids) for raw in raw_rules]

        self._downsample_ms = downsample_ms
        self._suppression_ms = suppression_ms
        self._enable_explanations = enable_explanations
        self._rules = rules
        self._registry = ExplanationRegistry() if registry is None else registry
        self._window_engine = WindowSuppressionEngine()
        if window_suppression_rules is not None:
            self._window_engine.set_rules(window_suppression_rules)
        # Maintenance-window configuration is validated up front; reset()
        # clears data but keeps it, exactly like the window rules above.
        self._maintenance_windows = _validate_maintenance_windows(maintenance_windows)
        self.reset()

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Drop all applied batches, samples, windows and alerts."""
        self._batches: dict = {}  # batch_id -> batch record
        self._retracted: set = set()  # batch_ids in the terminal retracted state
        # Each point keeps one candidate per contributing batch rank so that
        # retracting the winning batch can restore the next-highest rank.
        self._points: dict = {}  # point_key -> {rank: metric}
        self._bucket_points: dict = {}  # bucket_key -> set of point_key
        self._buckets: dict = {}  # bucket_key -> {sum, count, sources}
        self._alerts: list = []
        self._alert_ids: set = set()
        self._registry.clear()
        # Recorded window-suppression episodes are state, the configured rules
        # are not: reset clears the former and keeps the latter.
        self._window_engine.reset()

    # -- validation ---------------------------------------------------------

    def _validate_sample(self, raw: Any) -> dict:
        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
            raise BatchError(400, "metric_batch_invalid", "invalid metric")
        # A sample whose timestamp is not a usable epoch-millis value cannot be
        # assigned to any downsample window; it must not be dropped silently.
        if not _valid_timestamp(raw.get("timestamp_ms")):
            raise BatchError(422, "metric_window_unresolved", "metric window unresolved")
        try:
            return _validate_metric(raw)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise BatchError(400, "metric_batch_invalid", str(exc)) from exc

    # -- batch application --------------------------------------------------

    def apply_batch(self, request: dict) -> dict:
        """Apply one metric batch, or delegate legacy requests to ``process``.

        A request without ``batch_id`` is handled by the original stateless
        entry point with unchanged behavior. With ``batch_id`` the batch is
        validated as a whole, deduplicated by content, and merged into the
        stored streams; affected windows are recomputed immediately.
        """
        if not isinstance(request, dict):
            raise BatchError(400, "metric_batch_invalid", "invalid request")
        batch_id = request.get("batch_id")
        if batch_id is None:
            return process(request)
        if not (isinstance(batch_id, str) and batch_id != ""):
            raise BatchError(400, "metric_batch_invalid", "invalid batch_id")

        # Per-query source failover is never part of a batch: applying (or
        # retracting) a batch must neither persist nor silently accept it.
        if "source_priority" in request:
            raise BatchError(400, "metric_batch_invalid", "invalid source_priority")

        max_event_time_ms = request.get("max_event_time_ms")
        if not _valid_timestamp(max_event_time_ms):
            raise BatchError(400, "metric_batch_invalid", "invalid max_event_time_ms")

        # Optional window-suppression reconfiguration: validated up front and
        # applied only once the whole batch has been accepted, taking effect
        # before this batch's events are recorded.
        raw_window_rules = request.get("window_suppression_rules")
        validated_window_rules: list | None = None
        if raw_window_rules is not None:
            validated_window_rules = _validate_window_rules(raw_window_rules)

        raw_metrics = request.get("metrics")
        if not isinstance(raw_metrics, list):
            raise BatchError(400, "metric_batch_invalid", "invalid request")
        metrics = [self._validate_sample(raw) for raw in raw_metrics]

        raw_alerts = request.get("alerts", [])
        if raw_alerts is None:
            raw_alerts = []
        if not isinstance(raw_alerts, list):
            raise BatchError(400, "metric_batch_invalid", "invalid request")
        seen_ids: set = set()
        alerts = []
        for raw in raw_alerts:
            try:
                alerts.append(_validate_alert(raw, seen_ids))
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise BatchError(400, "metric_batch_invalid", str(exc))

        fingerprint = _batch_fingerprint(max_event_time_ms, metrics, alerts)
        known = self._batches.get(batch_id)
        if known is not None:
            # The idempotency/conflict decision precedes the cross-batch
            # alert-id guard: re-posting an identical batch whose alerts are
            # already stored must report success without adding anything, and
            # a changed batch under the same id is always a conflict.
            if known["fingerprint"] == fingerprint:
                return {
                    "batch_id": batch_id,
                    "status": BATCH_APPLIED,
                    "affected_streams": 0,
                    "recomputed_windows": 0,
                }
            raise BatchError(409, "metric_batch_conflict", "metric batch conflict")
        # A retracted batch left no contributions behind, so re-applying the
        # same batch_id is a fresh application (the typical patch flow: retract
        # the faulty batch, then resubmit its correction under the same id).

        if any(alert["alert_id"] in self._alert_ids for alert in alerts):
            raise BatchError(400, "metric_batch_invalid", "duplicate alert_id")

        if metrics:
            if self._downsample_ms is None:
                raise BatchError(422, "metric_window_unresolved", "metric window unresolved")
            window_start = (max_event_time_ms // self._downsample_ms) * self._downsample_ms
            for metric in metrics:
                timestamp_ms = metric["timestamp_ms"]
                if timestamp_ms < window_start or timestamp_ms > max_event_time_ms:
                    raise BatchError(
                        400, "metric_batch_range_invalid", "metric batch range invalid"
                    )

        rank = (max_event_time_ms, batch_id)
        # Within one batch, identical points dedupe with the later one winning.
        batch_points: dict = {}
        for metric in metrics:
            point_key = (
                metric["source"],
                metric["name"],
                _canonical_labels(metric["labels"]),
                metric["timestamp_ms"],
            )
            batch_points[point_key] = metric

        affected_streams: set = set()
        affected_buckets: set = set()
        for point_key, metric in batch_points.items():
            candidates = self._points.setdefault(point_key, {})
            if rank in candidates:
                # Same rank tuple cannot occur for a different batch_id (the
                # batch_id is part of the rank) and duplicate batches were
                # handled above; nothing to merge in that case.
                continue
            winning_before = max(candidates) if candidates else None
            candidates[rank] = metric
            labels_key = point_key[2]
            start = (point_key[3] // self._downsample_ms) * self._downsample_ms
            bucket_key = (point_key[1], labels_key, start)
            self._bucket_points.setdefault(bucket_key, set()).add(point_key)
            if winning_before is None or rank > winning_before:
                # Only a newly winning value changes the aggregate/stream.
                affected_streams.add((point_key[1], labels_key))
                affected_buckets.add(bucket_key)

        for bucket_key in affected_buckets:
            self._recompute_bucket(bucket_key)

        self._batches[batch_id] = {
            "fingerprint": fingerprint,
            "rank": rank,
            "points": batch_points,
            "alerts": alerts,
        }
        self._retracted.discard(batch_id)
        self._alerts.extend(alerts)
        self._alert_ids.update(alert["alert_id"] for alert in alerts)

        if validated_window_rules is not None:
            self._window_engine.set_rules(validated_window_rules)
        if self._window_engine.rules:
            # Window-suppression episodes follow the event stream as observed;
            # retraction does not rewrite this history.
            _feed_window_events(
                self._window_engine, list(batch_points.values()), alerts
            )
        return {
            "batch_id": batch_id,
            "status": BATCH_APPLIED,
            "affected_streams": len(affected_streams),
            "recomputed_windows": len(affected_buckets),
        }

    def _point_winner(self, point_key: tuple) -> tuple | None:
        """Return ``(rank, metric)`` of the highest-rank candidate, if any."""
        candidates = self._points.get(point_key)
        if not candidates:
            return None
        rank = max(candidates)
        return rank, candidates[rank]

    def _recompute_bucket(self, bucket_key: tuple) -> None:
        bucket = _new_bucket()
        live_points = set()
        for point_key in self._bucket_points[bucket_key]:
            winner = self._point_winner(point_key)
            if winner is None:
                continue
            live_points.add(point_key)
            _rank, metric = winner
            _bucket_add(bucket, metric["source"], metric["timestamp_ms"], metric["value"])
        if bucket["count"] == 0:
            # No winning samples remain: the window disappears from queries.
            self._bucket_points.pop(bucket_key, None)
            self._buckets.pop(bucket_key, None)
            return
        self._bucket_points[bucket_key] = live_points
        self._buckets[bucket_key] = bucket

    # -- batch retraction ---------------------------------------------------

    def retract_batch(self, batch_id: Any) -> dict:
        """Retract a previously applied batch and correct the current state.

        The batch's deduplicated points and alerts stop contributing. Points
        shared with other batches re-resolve to the highest remaining batch
        rank; affected windows recompute under the same rank semantics. A
        second retraction of the same id is an idempotent no-op that still
        reports ``retracted`` with zero counts.
        """
        if not (isinstance(batch_id, str) and batch_id != ""):
            raise BatchError(
                400, "metric_batch_retract_invalid", "invalid batch_id"
            )
        if batch_id in self._retracted:
            return {
                "batch_id": batch_id,
                "status": BATCH_RETRACTED,
                "removed_metrics": 0,
                "removed_alerts": 0,
                "affected_streams": 0,
                "recomputed_windows": 0,
            }
        record = self._batches.get(batch_id)
        if record is None:
            raise BatchError(404, "metric_batch_not_found", "metric batch not found")

        rank = record["rank"]
        batch_points = record["points"]
        alerts = record["alerts"]

        # Identify every window the batch contributed candidates to and
        # snapshot its aggregate. Everything below is in-memory bookkeeping
        # that cannot fail, so retraction either commits fully or (on the
        # validation failures above) never starts.
        affected_buckets: set = set()
        for point_key in batch_points:
            labels_key = point_key[2]
            start = (point_key[3] // self._downsample_ms) * self._downsample_ms
            affected_buckets.add((point_key[1], labels_key, start))

        before_windows = {
            bucket_key: self._window_value(bucket_key) for bucket_key in affected_buckets
        }

        for point_key in batch_points:
            candidates = self._points.get(point_key)
            if candidates is None or rank not in candidates:
                continue
            del candidates[rank]
            if not candidates:
                self._points.pop(point_key, None)

        for alert in alerts:
            try:
                self._alerts.remove(alert)
            except ValueError:
                pass
            self._alert_ids.discard(alert["alert_id"])

        # Re-resolve winners among the remaining batch ranks. A window whose
        # higher-rank batch still covers a point keeps exactly its value; only
        # windows whose aggregate value changed (or that are cleared) count.
        changed_windows: set = set()
        for bucket_key, before in before_windows.items():
            self._recompute_bucket(bucket_key)
            if self._window_value(bucket_key) != before:
                changed_windows.add(bucket_key)

        changed_streams = {(key[0], key[1]) for key in changed_windows}

        self._batches.pop(batch_id, None)
        self._retracted.add(batch_id)

        return {
            "batch_id": batch_id,
            "status": BATCH_RETRACTED,
            "removed_metrics": len(batch_points),
            "removed_alerts": len(alerts),
            "affected_streams": len(changed_streams),
            "recomputed_windows": len(changed_windows),
        }

    def _window_value(self, bucket_key: tuple):
        """The query-visible aggregate value of a window, or None if it is gone.

        Only this value decides whether retraction changed observable output:
        count/source differences behind an identical mean change nothing.
        """
        bucket = self._buckets.get(bucket_key)
        if bucket is None:
            return None
        return round(bucket["sum"] / bucket["count"] + 0.0, 6)

    # -- late-sample recomputation --------------------------------------------

    def submit_late_metrics(self, request: Any) -> dict:
        """Apply late-arriving metric samples and recompute the windows they touch.

        ``request`` is a list of samples or a mapping with a ``"metrics"``
        list; each sample keeps the established metric fields
        (``source/name/labels/timestamp_ms/value``). A sample is late when it
        reaches the service after its downsample window has already been
        computed from earlier input. The window holding its timestamp is
        recomputed from the current sample set, so subsequent queries read the
        corrected window value, window time and source contributions; windows
        the samples do not touch keep their established results.

        The dedupe identity is the established
        ``source/name/labels/timestamp_ms`` point. Re-submitting an identical
        sample is an idempotent no-op (no double counting, no new alerts);
        the same identity carrying a different value is a conflict, rejected
        with a 400 ``late_metric_conflict`` error that leaves the established
        window results untouched. A missing or unparseable timestamp is a 400
        ``late_metric_invalid`` error; a timestamp outside the retained range
        (the span of downsample windows holding currently stored samples) is a
        404 ``late_metric_out_of_retention`` error. Validation is completed
        before any state changes, so every failure is atomic and neither
        aggregates nor alert states are modified.
        """
        if isinstance(request, dict):
            raw_metrics = request.get("metrics")
        else:
            raw_metrics = request
        if not isinstance(raw_metrics, list):
            raise BatchError(400, "late_metric_invalid", "invalid request")
        metrics = []
        for raw in raw_metrics:
            if not isinstance(raw, dict):
                raise BatchError(400, "late_metric_invalid", "invalid metric")
            # A sample whose timestamp is missing or unparseable cannot be
            # assigned to any downsample window; it must not be dropped
            # silently.
            if not _valid_timestamp(raw.get("timestamp_ms")):
                raise BatchError(400, "late_metric_invalid", "invalid timestamp")
            try:
                metrics.append(_validate_metric(raw))
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise BatchError(400, "late_metric_invalid", str(exc)) from exc

        if metrics and self._downsample_ms is None:
            raise BatchError(422, "metric_window_unresolved", "metric window unresolved")

        if metrics:
            # The retained range spans the downsample windows of every
            # currently stored sample; a late sample outside it can no longer
            # be assigned to a retained window.
            downsample_ms = self._downsample_ms
            timestamps = [point_key[3] for point_key in self._points]
            if not timestamps:
                raise BatchError(
                    404, "late_metric_out_of_retention", "late metric out of retention"
                )
            retention_start = (min(timestamps) // downsample_ms) * downsample_ms
            retention_end = (max(timestamps) // downsample_ms) * downsample_ms + downsample_ms
            for metric in metrics:
                timestamp_ms = metric["timestamp_ms"]
                if timestamp_ms < retention_start or timestamp_ms >= retention_end:
                    raise BatchError(
                        404,
                        "late_metric_out_of_retention",
                        "late metric out of retention",
                    )

        # Deduplicate by the established point identity — within the request
        # and against the stored winning samples. Any conflicting value is
        # rejected before anything is applied.
        unique: dict = {}
        duplicates = 0
        for metric in metrics:
            point_key = (
                metric["source"],
                metric["name"],
                _canonical_labels(metric["labels"]),
                metric["timestamp_ms"],
            )
            known = unique.get(point_key)
            if known is not None:
                if known["value"] != metric["value"]:
                    raise BatchError(400, "late_metric_conflict", "late metric conflict")
                duplicates += 1
                continue
            unique[point_key] = metric

        accepted: dict = {}
        for point_key, metric in unique.items():
            winner = self._point_winner(point_key)
            if winner is None:
                accepted[point_key] = metric
                continue
            _rank, existing = winner
            if existing["value"] != metric["value"]:
                raise BatchError(400, "late_metric_conflict", "late metric conflict")
            # An identical sample is already established: idempotent no-op.
            duplicates += 1

        affected_streams: set = set()
        affected_buckets: set = set()
        for point_key, metric in accepted.items():
            candidates = self._points.setdefault(point_key, {})
            candidates[_LATE_RANK] = metric
            start = (point_key[3] // self._downsample_ms) * self._downsample_ms
            bucket_key = (point_key[1], point_key[2], start)
            self._bucket_points.setdefault(bucket_key, set()).add(point_key)
            affected_streams.add((point_key[1], point_key[2]))
            affected_buckets.add(bucket_key)
        for bucket_key in affected_buckets:
            self._recompute_bucket(bucket_key)

        if accepted and self._window_engine.rules:
            # Late observations drive the window-suppression engine exactly
            # like batch events; identical resubmissions never reach here, so
            # no episode is recorded twice.
            _feed_window_events(self._window_engine, list(accepted.values()), [])

        return {
            "accepted": len(accepted),
            "duplicates": duplicates,
            "affected_streams": len(affected_streams),
            "recomputed_windows": len(affected_buckets),
        }

    # -- queries --------------------------------------------------------------

    def query_series(
        self,
        name: str | None = None,
        labels: dict | None = None,
        start_ms: Any = None,
        end_ms: Any = None,
        aggregations: dict | None = None,
        source_quorum: dict | None = None,
        source_weights: dict | None = None,
        source_priority: dict | None = None,
        gap_fill: dict | None = None,
        downsample_overrides: dict | None = None,
        source_outliers: dict | None = None,
    ) -> list:
        """Return current downsampled windows in the established output shape.

        Optional filters: exact metric name, label subset match, and a
        ``[start_ms, end_ms]`` range over window start times. ``aggregations``
        maps exact metric names to one of ``avg``/``min``/``max``/``sum``/
        ``last``/``median``/``p95``/``p99``; unmapped metrics keep the default
        ``avg``. ``median`` averages the two middle values for an even sample
        count; ``p95``/``p99`` use the one-based nearest rank ``ceil(q*n)``
        without interpolation. ``source_quorum`` maps exact
        metric names to positive integers: a window is output only when its
        deduplicated source set reaches the threshold. ``source_weights`` maps
        exact metric names to per-source weight configurations: a listed
        target merges each window as the weighted sum of its participating
        samples divided by the effective weight sum, and windows without
        effective weight are marked ``weight_missing`` with a null value.
        ``source_priority`` maps exact metric names to ordered source lists:
        a quorum-passing window of such a target uses only the first configured
        source that actually appears in the window (failover), aggregating
        that source's samples; windows with none of the configured sources are
        marked ``priority_missing`` with a null value. The same metric may not
        appear in both ``source_weights`` and ``source_priority``.
        ``gap_fill`` maps exact metric names to a positive integer
        ``max_gap_ms``: after all of the above, missing windows between two
        adjacent output windows of the same normalized series are filled
        (value carried over from the previous window, ``count`` 0, empty
        ``sources``) whenever the gap does not exceed ``max_gap_ms``; windows
        dropped by ``source_quorum`` are never resurrected, and nothing is
        filled before the first or after the last output window.
        ``downsample_overrides`` maps exact metric names to positive integer
        millisecond periods: a listed metric's windows are recomputed from
        the current winning samples with ``timestamp_ms // period * period``
        as the window start (so patches, late corrections and retractions are
        reflected), while unlisted metrics keep the windows computed with the
        service's ``downsample_ms``. Gap filling uses each metric's own
        period; different metrics never align to a common grid. Batch
        application and retraction keep using the service ``downsample_ms``
        for ranges, ranks and affected-window accounting regardless of this
        mapping. ``source_outliers`` maps exact metric names to
        ``{"min_sources", "tolerance"}`` filters: within each window of a
        listed metric, every source's representative value (the mean of its
        deduplicated winning samples) is compared against the median of the
        representatives, and once the window's source count reaches
        ``min_sources`` any source differing by strictly more than
        ``tolerance`` is dropped as a whole before aggregation, weighting,
        failover, quorum and gap filling are applied — so patches, late
        corrections and retractions are re-filtered from the current winning
        samples on every query. Metrics absent from the mapping are
        unaffected. Output rows keep the existing fields and the existing
        (name, labels, timestamp) order.
        """
        if name is not None and not isinstance(name, str):
            raise ValueError("invalid name")
        if labels is not None and not isinstance(labels, dict):
            raise ValueError("invalid labels")
        for bound in (start_ms, end_ms):
            if bound is not None and not _valid_timestamp(bound):
                raise ValueError("invalid time range")
        agg_map = _validate_aggregations(aggregations)
        quorum_map = _validate_source_quorum(source_quorum)
        weights_map = _validate_source_weights(source_weights)
        priority_map = _validate_source_priority(source_priority)
        if priority_map.keys() & weights_map.keys():
            raise ValueError("invalid source_priority")
        gap_fill_map = _validate_gap_fill(gap_fill)
        override_map = _validate_downsample_overrides(downsample_overrides)
        outliers_map = _validate_source_outliers(source_outliers)

        if override_map:
            # Metrics with an override are re-windowed from the current
            # winning samples; every other metric keeps the stored buckets.
            buckets = {
                key: bucket
                for key, bucket in self._buckets.items()
                if key[0] not in override_map
            }
            for point_key in self._points:
                point_name = point_key[1]
                period = override_map.get(point_name)
                if period is None:
                    continue
                winner = self._point_winner(point_key)
                if winner is None:
                    continue
                _rank, metric = winner
                timestamp_ms = point_key[3]
                start = (timestamp_ms // period) * period
                bucket_key = (point_name, point_key[2], start)
                bucket = buckets.get(bucket_key)
                if bucket is None:
                    bucket = _new_bucket()
                    buckets[bucket_key] = bucket
                _bucket_add(bucket, metric["source"], timestamp_ms, metric["value"])
        else:
            buckets = self._buckets

        rows = []
        quorum_blocked: set = set()
        for (bucket_name, labels_key, start), bucket in buckets.items():
            if name is not None and bucket_name != name:
                continue
            bucket_labels = json.loads(labels_key)
            if labels is not None and any(
                bucket_labels.get(key) != value for key, value in labels.items()
            ):
                continue
            if start_ms is not None and start < start_ms:
                continue
            if end_ms is not None and start > end_ms:
                continue
            # Source-outlier filtering runs on the window's current winning
            # samples before coverage, aggregation, weighting or failover;
            # a window whose samples are all filtered out produces no row.
            outlier_config = outliers_map.get(bucket_name)
            if outlier_config is not None:
                bucket = _filter_source_outliers(
                    bucket, outlier_config["min_sources"], outlier_config["tolerance"]
                )
                if bucket["count"] == 0:
                    continue
            # Coverage is the size of the full deduplicated winning-sample
            # source set, recomputed from current winners after every patch or
            # retraction — not the sample or request count.
            if (
                bucket_name in quorum_map
                and len(bucket["sources"]) < quorum_map[bucket_name]
            ):
                quorum_blocked.add((bucket_name, labels_key, start))
                continue
            weights = weights_map.get(bucket_name)
            if weights is not None:
                rows.append(_weighted_row(bucket_name, labels_key, start, bucket, weights))
                continue
            priorities = priority_map.get(bucket_name)
            if priorities is not None:
                rows.append(
                    _priority_row(
                        bucket_name,
                        labels_key,
                        start,
                        bucket,
                        priorities,
                        agg_map.get(bucket_name, "avg"),
                    )
                )
                continue
            rows.append(
                {
                    "name": bucket_name,
                    "labels": bucket_labels,
                    "timestamp_ms": start,
                    "value": _bucket_value(bucket, agg_map.get(bucket_name, "avg")),
                    "count": bucket["count"],
                    "sources": sorted(bucket["sources"]),
                }
            )
        rows.sort(key=lambda row: (row["name"], _canonical_labels(row["labels"]), row["timestamp_ms"]))
        if gap_fill_map and self._downsample_ms is not None:
            # A service without downsample_ms can never hold samples, so there
            # are no windows to fill between.
            rows = _fill_series_gaps(
                rows, self._downsample_ms, gap_fill_map, quorum_blocked, override_map
            )
        return rows

    # -- window suppression rules --------------------------------------------

    def set_window_suppression_rules(self, rules: list | None) -> None:
        """Replace the time-window suppression rule set (all or nothing).

        The new configuration governs events arriving after this call;
        changing durations never retroactively alters recorded hits, and
        removing a rule only stops future matching — its recorded states stay
        queryable by rule_id.
        """
        self._window_engine.set_rules(rules)

    def query_suppression_states(
        self,
        rule_id: str | None = None,
        source: str | None = None,
        labels: dict | None = None,
        now_ms: Any = None,
    ) -> list:
        """Return recorded window-suppression states (see ``WindowSuppressionEngine.query``)."""
        return self._window_engine.query(
            rule_id=rule_id, source=source, labels=labels, now_ms=now_ms
        )

    # -- maintenance windows ---------------------------------------------------

    @property
    def maintenance_windows(self) -> list:
        """The configured maintenance windows (defensive copies)."""
        return [
            dict(window, labels=dict(window["labels"]) if window["labels"] is not None else None)
            for window in self._maintenance_windows
        ]

    def set_maintenance_windows(self, windows: list | None) -> None:
        """Replace the maintenance-window configuration (all or nothing).

        Validation is fully completed before anything is replaced, so a
        rejected configuration leaves the previous one untouched. ``None``
        clears the configuration.
        """
        self._maintenance_windows = _validate_maintenance_windows(windows)

    def query_alerts(self) -> dict:
        """Re-adjudicate all stored alerts against the current configuration.

        Suppression is recomputed on every query, so corrections that change
        the stored alert set are reflected in subsequent results.
        """
        alerts = list(self._alerts)
        window_suppressed_ids = {
            alert["alert_id"]
            for alert in alerts
            if self._window_engine.is_suppressed(
                alert["source"], alert["name"], alert["labels"], alert["timestamp_ms"]
            )
        }
        # Maintenance windows are re-evaluated against the current alert set
        # on every query, so late corrections and retractions are reflected.
        extra_suppressed_ids = window_suppressed_ids | _maintenance_suppressed_ids(
            alerts, self._maintenance_windows
        )
        if self._enable_explanations:
            result, _rule_hits = _process_with_explanations(
                alerts, self.query_series(), self._rules, self._registry
            )
            if extra_suppressed_ids:
                for output_alert in result["alerts"]:
                    if output_alert["alert_id"] in extra_suppressed_ids:
                        output_alert["status"] = "suppressed"
                merged_ids = set(result["suppressed_alert_ids"]) | extra_suppressed_ids
                result["suppressed_alert_ids"] = [
                    output_alert["alert_id"]
                    for output_alert in result["alerts"]
                    if output_alert["alert_id"] in merged_ids
                ]
            return result
        result_alerts, suppressed_alert_ids, _time_ids = _suppress_alerts(
            alerts, self._suppression_ms
        )
        if extra_suppressed_ids:
            for entry in result_alerts:
                if entry["alert_id"] in extra_suppressed_ids:
                    entry["suppressed"] = True
            suppressed_alert_ids = [
                entry["alert_id"] for entry in result_alerts if entry["suppressed"]
            ]
        return {"alerts": result_alerts, "suppressed_alert_ids": suppressed_alert_ids}

    def query_suppression_audit(self) -> list:
        """Re-adjudicate all stored alerts and return one audit record each.

        Like ``query_alerts`` the verdict is recomputed against the current
        stored alert set, so batch patches, late corrections and retractions
        are reflected; the query itself mutates no state (it never writes
        explanation records). Records follow stored-alert order; causes are
        ordered by kind (time, suppression_rule, window_rule, maintenance)
        with ids sorted lexicographically within a kind.
        """
        alerts = list(self._alerts)
        _result_alerts, _time_list, time_suppressed_ids = _suppress_alerts(
            alerts, self._suppression_ms
        )
        window_hits_by_id: dict = {}
        for alert in alerts:
            hit_rules = self._window_engine.suppressing_rules(
                alert["source"], alert["name"], alert["labels"], alert["timestamp_ms"]
            )

9	import argparse
10	import json
11	import threading
12	from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
13	from urllib.parse import parse_qs, unquote, urlsplit
14

16	    BatchError,

22	)

24	RETRACT_PREFIX = "/v1/metric_batches/"
25	RETRACT_SUFFIX = "/retract"
26	LATE_METRICS_PATH = "/v1/late_metrics"
27	WINDOW_RULES_PATH = "/v1/window_suppression_rules"
28	WINDOW_SUPPRESSIONS_PATH = "/v1/window_suppressions"
29	SUPPRESSION_AUDIT_PATH = "/v1/suppression_audit"

32	
33	def _send_json(handler: BaseHTTPRequestHandler, status: int, payload: dict) -> None:
34	    body = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
35	    handler.send_response(status)
36	    handler.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
37	    handler.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
38	    handler.end_headers()
39	    handler.wfile.write(body)
40	
41	
42	def _send_error(handler: BaseHTTPRequestHandler, status: int, code: str, message: str) -> None:
43	    _send_json(handler, status, {"code": code, "message": message})
44	
45	
46	def _make_handler(service: MetricBatchService, lock: threading.Lock):
47	    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
48	        def _read_json(self) -> dict:
49	            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
50	            raw = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b""
51	            try:
52	                return json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8") or "null")
53	            except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
54	                raise BatchError(400, "invalid_request", "invalid JSON")
55	
56	        def _handle_batch(self) -> None:
57	            try:
58	                with lock:
59	                    result = service.apply_batch(self._read_json())
60	            except BatchError as exc:
61	                _send_error(self, exc.status, exc.code, str(exc))
62	            except RuleConfigurationError as exc:
63	                _send_error(self, 400, "rule_configuration_error", str(exc))
64	            except MaintenanceWindowError as exc:
65	                _send_error(self, 400, "invalid_maintenance_window", str(exc))
66	            except ValueError as exc:  # legacy path validation errors
67	                _send_error(self, 400, "invalid_request", str(exc))
68	            else:
69	                _send_json(self, 200, result)
70	
71	        def _handle_late_metrics(self) -> None:
72	            try:
73	                with lock:
74	                    result = service.submit_late_metrics(self._read_json())
75	            except BatchError as exc:
76	                _send_error(self, exc.status, exc.code, str(exc))
77	            else:
78	                _send_json(self, 200, result)
79	
80	        def _handle_window_rules(self) -> None:
81	            try:
82	                body = self._read_json()
83	                rules = body.get("rules") if isinstance(body, dict) else body
84	                with lock:
85	                    service.set_window_suppression_rules(rules)
86	            except BatchError as exc:
87	                _send_error(self, exc.status, exc.code, str(exc))
88	            except RuleConfigurationError as exc:
89	                _send_error(self, 400, "rule_configuration_error", str(exc))
90	            else:
91	                _send_json(self, 200, {"status": "ok"})
92	
93	        def _handle_maintenance_windows(self) -> None:
94	            try:
95	                body = self._read_json()
96	                windows = body.get("maintenance_windows") if isinstance(body, dict) else body
97	                with lock:
98	                    service.set_maintenance_windows(windows)
99	            except BatchError as exc:

101	            except MaintenanceWindowError as exc:

103	            else:

105	
106	        def _retract_batch_id(self, path: str) -> str | None:
107	            """Extract a batch_id from the retract path, or None if malformed.
108	
109	            The accepted shape is exactly
110	            ``/v1/metric_batches/{batch_id}/retract`` with a single non-empty
111	            path segment as the id; percent-encoding is decoded.
112	            """
113	            if not (path.startswith(RETRACT_PREFIX) and path.endswith(RETRACT_SUFFIX)):
114	                return None
115	            middle = path[len(RETRACT_PREFIX):-len(RETRACT_SUFFIX)]
116	            if middle == "" or "/" in middle:
117	                return None
118	            return unquote(middle)
119	
120	        def _handle_retract(self, batch_id: str) -> None:
121	            # A request body is optional; if present it must be recognizable
122	            # JSON rather than an opaque payload.
123	            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
124	            raw = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b""
125	            if raw.strip():
126	                try:
127	                    parsed = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
128	                except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
129	                    _send_error(
130	                        self,
131	                        400,
132	                        "metric_batch_retract_invalid",
133	                        "invalid request",
134	                    )
135	                    return
136	                # Query-time source failover is never accepted by batch
137	                # operations: only query_series reads source_priority.
138	                if isinstance(parsed, dict) and "source_priority" in parsed:
139	                    _send_error(
140	                        self,
141	                        400,
142	                        "metric_batch_retract_invalid",
143	                        "invalid source_priority",
144	                    )
145	                    return
146	            try:
147	                with lock:
148	                    result = service.retract_batch(batch_id)
149	            except BatchError as exc:
150	                _send_error(self, exc.status, exc.code, str(exc))
151	            else:
152	                _send_json(self, 200, result)
153	
154	        def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - stdlib handler API
155	            path = urlsplit(self.path).path
156	            if path == "/v1/metric_batches":
157	                self._handle_batch()
158	            elif path == LATE_METRICS_PATH:
159	                self._handle_late_metrics()
160	            elif path == WINDOW_RULES_PATH:
161	                self._handle_window_rules()
162	            elif path == MAINTENANCE_WINDOWS_PATH:
163	                self._handle_maintenance_windows()
164	            elif path.startswith(RETRACT_PREFIX):
165	                batch_id = self._retract_batch_id(path)
166	                if batch_id is None:
167	                    _send_error(
168	                        self,
169	                        400,
170	                        "metric_batch_retract_invalid",
171	                        "invalid batch_id",
172	                    )
173	                else:
174	                    self._handle_retract(batch_id)
175	            elif self.path == "/process":
176	                try:
177	                    result = process(self._read_json())
178	                except BatchError as exc:
179	                    _send_error(self, exc.status, exc.code, str(exc))
180	                except RuleConfigurationError as exc:
181	                    _send_error(self, 400, "rule_configuration_error", str(exc))
182	                except EventTimestampError as exc:
183	                    _send_error(self, 400, "event_timestamp_error", str(exc))
184	                except MaintenanceWindowError as exc:
185	                    _send_error(self, 400, "invalid_maintenance_window", str(exc))
186	                except ValueError as exc:
187	                    _send_error(self, 400, "invalid_request", str(exc))
188	                else:
189	                    _send_json(self, 200, result)
190	            elif self.path == "/v1/query":
191	                try:
192	                    body = self._read_json()
193	                    if not isinstance(body, dict):
194	                        raise ValueError("invalid request")
195	                    with lock:
196	                        series = service.query_series(
197	                            name=body.get("name"),
198	                            labels=body.get("labels"),
199	                            start_ms=body.get("start_ms"),
200	                            end_ms=body.get("end_ms"),
201	                            aggregations=body.get("aggregations"),
202	                            source_quorum=body.get("source_quorum"),
203	                            source_weights=body.get("source_weights"),
204	                            source_priority=body.get("source_priority"),
205	                            gap_fill=body.get("gap_fill"),
206	                            downsample_overrides=body.get("downsample_overrides"),
207	                            source_outliers=body.get("source_outliers"),
208	                        )
209	                except BatchError as exc:
210	                    _send_error(self, exc.status, exc.code, str(exc))
211	                except ValueError as exc:
212	                    _send_error(self, 400, "invalid_request", str(exc))
213	                else:
214	                    _send_json(self, 200, {"series": series})
215	            else:
216	                _send_error(self, 404, "not_found", "not found")
217	
218	        def do_PUT(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - stdlib handler API
219	            path = urlsplit(self.path).path
220	            if path == WINDOW_RULES_PATH:
221	                self._handle_window_rules()
222	            elif path == MAINTENANCE_WINDOWS_PATH:
223	                self._handle_maintenance_windows()
224	            else:
225	                _send_error(self, 404, "not_found", "not found")
226	
227	        def do_GET(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - stdlib handler API
228	            split = urlsplit(self.path)
229	            if split.path == WINDOW_SUPPRESSIONS_PATH:
230	                params = parse_qs(split.query)
231	                now_raw = params.get("now_ms", [None])[0]
232	                try:
233	                    now_ms = float(now_raw) if now_raw is not None else None
234	                except ValueError:
235	                    _send_error(
236	                        self, 400, "event_timestamp_error", "unsortable event timestamp"
237	                    )
238	                    return
239	                try:
240	                    with lock:
241	                        states = service.query_suppression_states(
242	                            rule_id=params.get("rule_id", [None])[0],
243	                            source=params.get("source", [None])[0],
244	                            now_ms=now_ms,
245	                        )
246	                except EventTimestampError as exc:
247	                    _send_error(self, 400, "event_timestamp_error", str(exc))
248	                else:
249	                    _send_json(self, 200, {"suppression_states": states})
250	            elif self.path == "/v1/alerts":
251	                with lock:
252	                    _send_json(self, 200, service.query_alerts())
253	            elif split.path == SUPPRESSION_AUDIT_PATH:
254	                # Read-only: the audit is re-adjudicated like GET /v1/alerts
255	                # but changes neither alerts, series nor configuration state.
256	                with lock:
257	                    _send_json(
258	                        self, 200, {"suppression_audit": service.query_suppression_audit()}
259	                    )
260	            elif self.path == "/v1/series":
261	                with lock:
262	                    _send_json(self, 200, {"series": service.query_series()})
263	            else:
264	                _send_error(self, 404, "not_found", "not found")

266	        def log_message(self, *args) -> None:  # keep the server quiet by default
267	            pass

272	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
273	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m metric_fusion.server")
274	    parser.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
